description: Machine-readable registry of CI-pinned documentation behavior claims (the claims-fixture gate, ADR-0023). Each claim states exactly what its named engine test pins - no more. The claim's normative sentence must appear on one of its pages (check 8 of scripts/check-doc-canon.py: whitespace-normalized, case-insensitive containment) and the engine test pin must exist and pass in the normal build. Origin: the AI grammar coverage study found all documentation drift in ungated prose - this gate extends drift testing from shape to behavior. An AI agent may treat these claims as source-verified.

claims.claim: The flow exception context exposes the HTTP status under error.code.
claims.quote: error.code - the status code of the exception

claims.claim: When application.properties and application.yml define the same key, the .yml value wins (application.yml is merged last).
The Kafka flow adapter treats any flow reply status below 400 (2xx/3xx) as success - acknowledged, never retried or dead-lettered.
claims.quote: A flow **succeeds** when it replies with a status below `400`

claims.claim: Registering a duplicate route does not fail the application: the earlier registration is reloaded and the newest function serves.
claims.quote: a duplicate route reloads the earlier registration

claims.claim: @PreLoad envInstances names a configuration KEY looked up in application.properties; a nonexistent key falls back to the annotation's instances.
claims.quote: envInstances names a property key looked up in

claims.claim: A flows.yaml manifest that omits 'location' loads its flow files from classpath:/flows/.
A non-boolean, non-numeric decision value coerces to 1 and silently selects the first branch.
The Playground inspect command resolves whole subtrees, not only leaf keys.
Graph export does not reject orphan nodes; the CompileGraph deployment gate re-validates the whole model.
claims.quote: Orphan nodes are not rejected at export

claims.claim: The reserved model-metadata key set is exactly nine names: cid, instance, flow, ttl, trace, parent, root, none, run.
rest.yaml's stream: true is parsed by the engine and streaming replies ride a dedicated ordered reply lane.
claims.quote: progressive response streaming (SSE / chunked JSON Lines) on a dedicated ordered reply lane
